identity.title: A Representer Theorem for Hawkes Processes via Penalized Least Squares Minimization

problem.claim: Estimate latent triggering kernels for linear multivariate Hawkes processes from observed event sequences in an RKHS framework.

contributions.claim: Derives a representer theorem for penalized least-squares estimation in which transformed kernels satisfy simultaneous integral equations and optimal triggering-kernel estimators are data-point expansions.
Fixes all dual coefficients analytically to unity, avoiding coefficient optimization and yielding an efficient estimator for large-scale data.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper reports a novel representer-theorem form based on transformed kernels defined through simultaneous integral equations, with analytically unit dual coefficients.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report competitive predictive accuracy and substantially improved computational efficiency on synthetic and real-world datasets versus state-of-the-art kernel-method estimators.
The authors report that unit dual coefficients eliminate the need to solve a costly optimization problem for those coefficients.

narrative_sequence.summary: Representer theorems reduce infinite-dimensional RKHS optimization to finite-dimensional dual-coefficient problems.
The paper targets estimation of Hawkes-process triggering kernels from observed event sequences.
It introduces transformed kernels governed by simultaneous integral equations, unit dual coefficients, and reported accuracy-efficiency results on synthetic and real-world data.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a structural theorem to an implementation simplification: transformed-kernel expansions are paired with analytically fixed unit coefficients.

lessons.interpretation: A theoretical characterization can be especially actionable when it removes a computational subproblem.
lessons.application: When presenting a new estimator, identify whether the derived structure analytically fixes or eliminates any learned quantities, and state the resulting computational consequence.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the supposedly fixed quantities depend on data, tuning choices, or conditions not established in the available evidence.

unknowns: The abstract does not state the assumptions under which the simultaneous integral equations, representer form, or unit coefficients hold.
Dataset sizes, computational metrics, baselines, and statistical uncertainty for the reported empirical comparison are unspecified.
The abstract does not detail the transformed kernels or the estimator’s limitations and tuning procedure.
